climb.rationale: Index of coincidence first, then the published n-gram counts, which is the ordering Ostwald and Weierud describe. Measured at 167 letters with ten pairs: n-grams alone from the identity plugboard recover the exact plugboard on 3 of 8 key draws; seeding with an index-of-coincidence climb recovers 8 of 8 for 1.6x the work.
climb.window_rationale: Fixed at W = 117 by the sweep rule preregistered in phase1-windowed-climb-power-v1 before that run, whose three deciding predictions held. W = 134 measured slightly higher on indel draws there; the rule forbids choosing it on that evidence.
climb.first_plug_rationale: Partial exhaustion of the first plug (Ostwald and Weierud 2017, section 7, the 'E-Stecker' method): the climb is run from the empty plugboard and from each of the 25 boards that plug E to another letter, and the best final n-gram score is kept, the earliest board winning a tie. Without it the climb is v4's exactly (the empty board is the first start). The reason is docs/code-review-2026-10-11.md B-1: the repository's power controls used one plaintext of IC 0.0792, Army traffic averages about 0.061, and detection falls steeply with plaintext IC because the first climb phase is an index-of-coincidence climb that traps. 26 starts cost 26 times the climbs.

positive_controls.rationale: The five independently solved 1941 Army plaintexts Phase 7 already uses, each kept as its own message with its own indicator and enciphered by enigma.EnigmaI under one shared ten-pair daily key. That is the real Army situation: several short messages under one key. An earlier version of this control concatenated the five into two messages at the target lengths and failed, because the junctions between unrelated messages are n-grams no Army text contains; the concatenated form was not a legitimate control and was replaced rather than reinterpreted.

key.plugboard: AV BS CG DL FU HZ IN KM OW RX

positive_controls.rationale: Three messages at exactly the target lengths 167, 107 and 97, from constructed Army-style text that cannot overlap the published n-gram counts. Trades authenticity for a guarantee of no training overlap, so the two controls fail in different ways if either weakness matters.

key.plugboard: AN BY CF DR GJ HS IL KM PV QZ

limitations: The controls are constructed or independently solved plaintexts, not authentic held-out Army traffic with an authentic daily key.

The messages behind the published 1941 n-gram counts are not enumerated, so overlap between the authentic control plaintexts and the scorer's training data cannot be ruled out. The constructed control exists to bound that risk, not to remove it.

The positive controls are body-direct and are handed the true wheel order, ring setting and start positions. They certify the stecker stage at the target lengths and say nothing about the rotor enumeration, which the sweeps and calibrations cover separately.

Every result assumes UKW-B, the Army/Air Force wheels I-V and the 1940+ clear-Grundstellung indicator procedure. A different reflector, a Naval wheel or a different indicator convention is outside every space searched here.
The calibrations use one plaintext per cell and a single key draw per cell. They locate the detection boundary to within a cell, not to a precise length.

The authentic control pools five short messages under one daily key (275 letters); the constructed control pools three at the target lengths (371 letters). Neither certifies a single 167-letter message on its own, which is what the capability calibration measures.

The middle-complete space has an exact equivalent for every daily key at 167 letters (rule_key_coverage 1.0). A key is still found only if the climb converges at one of its equivalents and scores into the top 100 of nine times as many settings as v3 searched; the stated power measures the first on planted draws and stands in for the second with a pooled null.

The companion calibration (phase1-companion-calibration-v1) was measured with middle-past-notch candidates. Under middle_complete a candidate's middle ring can put the notch inside a companion, and the companion check presents the candidate's rings as reported, so a companion whose true left wheel steps at a different letter is deciphered exactly only up to that letter. The joint figure in refuted_by includes that case at its natural rate on planted draws.
No result here is an accepted break: a confirmed candidate's plaintext still has to be read and reviewed before accepted_break could change.

The stated power is measured on planted single-indel and clean 167-letter draws through the complete rule's parameterization in the planted key's neighbourhood (phase1-middle-complete-power-v1), judged by a 6-sigma threshold over a pooled wrong-setting null. Under a normal null the top-100 retention cutoff over 246.8 million settings is about 4.9 sigma, below that threshold, but v2's and v3's maxima sat about 0.7 sigma above the normal expectation over 27.4 million, so the null's far tail is heavier than normal and the real cutoff is not measured. The joint companion figure was measured post hoc and preregistered nowhere.

The sweep scores each setting by the better of two 117-letter windows, so its scores are not on the scale of v2's whole-message scores; the indicator confirmation, which compares a pooled date score with the candidate's own sweep score, is reported but is even less informative here than in v2. The companion check alone decides.
A candidate found through the tail window is reported at the setting that deciphers the tail, which for a garbled message is one keystroke away from the setting of the head.

The power is conditional on v2 and v3 both null, with 'missed by both past-notch arms' on planted draws standing in for both sweeps being null, the same stand-in and the same limits as phase1-middle-complete-power-v1: one plaintext, a single indel only, 400 draws per cell, and strata of 57, 118 and 74 draws.

The prior q of one dropped or inserted letter is unmeasured. q = 0.2 is the value phase1-middle-complete-power-v1 declared; the stated power at other q is given in refuted_by so another belief can be applied without a rerun.

The cited paper (Sullivan and Weierud 2005, footnote 42) places Batch C on a different radio network and its authors suspect differently wired wheels. Every figure here assumes wheels I-V as wired; if that is wrong the power is zero and a null says nothing about these messages.

phase1-split-point-power-v1's yield model favoured a split-point sweep per host-hour at every prior (0.0059 against 0.0030 at q = 0.2) but its rule did not consult the yield model once S1 and S2 were both refuted. This sweep follows the rule as written; it is the more powerful single sweep, not the more efficient one.

Everything this sweep can say is about a standard Enigma I reading of BYQMZ with at most the faults the W = 117 head-and-tail climb tolerates (one dropped or inserted letter, a substituted letter); it does not search a split point and so is weaker than v5 for an indel in the middle third. It spends its extra cost on the plaintext's first plugs, not on faults.

The stated power comes from Markov plaintexts of the scorer's own counts, not authentic held-out Army traffic, and from a slice around a planted key, not the whole space; the E-start null (the best of 26 climbs) is heavier-tailed than the whole-message one, so the 6-sigma detection threshold of the control and the z = 6 companion threshold of the sweep are not the same quantity.
hypothesis: BYQMZ, FKQLZ and XFEDT of 1941-09-30 are Enigma I traffic (UKW-B, wheels I-V, ten stecker pairs) under one daily key, and BYQMZ's key is one that v4's sweep (the W = 117 head-and-tail climb over the middle-complete space) could miss because its plaintext has the typical, not the high, index of coincidence (about 0.06): at typical IC the climb from the empty plugboard is trapped far more often than the 0.8 to 0.9 rate measured under the one plaintext (IC 0.0792) behind the stated power of v2 to v5. The same complete sweep with partial exhaustion of the first plug (the E-Stecker start set, 26 boards) then retains at least one candidate that the companion-body confirmation accepts: FKQLZ and XFEDT each deciphered at all 17,576 starts under the candidate's wheel order, rings and plugboard, both best starts at z >= 6.
refuted_by: No retained candidate companion-confirmed. Stated power: the clean detection rate of the complete_w117_estecker arm of phase1-estecker-power-v1 over its 24 typical-IC plaintexts (480 draws), multiplied by the 96.6% of detections the v5 control confirmed, recorded in this configuration by amendment before the sweep launches, together with the arm's one-indel rate. The sweep is launched only if that control's P2 (E arm at least 75% of clean draws) and P3 (at least 20 points over v4's climb) held; if either is refuted the E-start set does not repair typical-IC power at this climb and this sweep is withdrawn unrun. A null here, at that stated power, multiplies the remaining odds of a standard Enigma I reading by about one minus the stated power, which is a statement about a typical-IC plaintext only: BYQMZ's own plaintext IC is unknown. Nothing here tests two faults, a substituted letter combined with another fault, other reflectors, other wheel wirings, Naval wheels, other indicator procedures or non-Enigma systems.

body_direct_sweep.rationale: Same message, ring rule (middle_complete), climb (W = 117), retention, start axes, right-ring axis, companions and threshold as v4, run on the cuda engine from the start; the only change is climb.first_plug = E. v4's 246,767,040 settings are swept again with 26 start boards each. Projected cost: v4 took 33 minutes on the RTX 3090, so about 14 hours (26 times; an inference to be replaced by the measured figure). 1,560 checkpointed chunks, so a stop loses at most one chunk.

predictions.statement: At least one of the 100 retained candidates is companion-confirmed (min over FKQLZ and XFEDT of best-start z >= 6).
If a candidate is confirmed, it is also the sweep's rank-1 candidate on BYQMZ alone.

Re-climbing each of v4's 100 retained settings with the E start set gives a score per letter at least v4's, to within 1e-9. The empty board is the first start and the climb from it is v4's exactly, so a fall would mean the implementation changed the climb. Checked after the run by a CPU re-climb of v4's retained rows.
All 100 retained candidates re-climb identically on the CPU batched climber (plugboard and score), as v5's did on the CPU SplitClimber.

If no candidate is confirmed, the sweep's top score lies between z = 5.5 and z = 8.0 over the distribution of all 246,767,040 settings' scores (v4 6.51). The upper bound is higher than v4's preregistered 7.5 because the best of 26 climbs has a heavier right tail than one.

pre_run_facts.disclosure: Everything below was known before this run and shaped this configuration. None of it is a result of this sweep.
pre_run_facts.review: docs/code-review-2026-10-11.md (measured there, not preregistered): detection of the whole-message climb falls with plaintext IC (r = 0.87 over 16 Markov plaintexts, IC 0.0514 to 0.0625); the v5 climb detects 3%, 20% and 57% at IC 0.0514, 0.0578 and 0.0625 against 97% at the repository's plaintext (IC 0.0792); the E-Stecker start set lifts the true-setting climb from 5/24 to 19/24 at IC 0.0578. Army plaintext averages IC about 0.061 (Ostwald and Weierud 2017).
pre_run_facts.power_control: phase1-estecker-power-v1 (preregistered in the same commit as this file) measures v4's climb with and without the E start set on 24 typical-IC plaintexts; this sweep's stated power is taken from it and its launch is conditional on its P2 and P3.
pre_run_facts.implementation: climb.first_plug (stecker_climb.start_boards, stecker_batch.BatchedClimber, the CUDA kernel's start loop). tests/test_first_plug.py pins reference, batched and cuda to identical plugboards, evaluation counts, scores and windows, and the run's preflight repeats that on this configuration (cuda_climb_parity and first_plug_climb_parity) before any search.
pre_run_facts.v4: phase1-body-direct-sweep-v4 is null: no retained candidate companion-confirmed (best z 4.69), top score the noise maximum (z 6.51), GPU run 2026-10-08. v5 (split-point) is null too (best companion z 4.84). Neither used a start set.
pre_run_facts.smoke_run: Before committing, this configuration was smoke-run once through the runner on a 72-setting slice (two wheel orders, scratch output and checkpoint, 5 min 35 s, nearly all of it the preflight and positive controls with 26 starts per climb). Preflight passed including first_plug_climbs_match and cuda_climb_matches_batched; both positive controls passed. No result of the slice was used for anything, and nothing was changed after it.

run_constraint: Not run. Run from a clean tree after this configuration, phase1-estecker-power-v1's result and its stated-power amendment are committed, on a host with nvcc and the GPU otherwise idle (the cuda engine ignores --jobs). The checkpoint under build/ (git-ignored; do not clean it while the sweep is unfinished) lets it be stopped and resumed by rerunning the same command. A resumed run repeats the preflight, the positive controls and both confirmations, and its artifact's timing fields cover only the last invocation, so record every start, stop and resume in the history.
